origin: copied from the Step 4 design document, section 8.1 and the 3.2.1 tables, 2026-10-13 (constant references already resolved)

data.run_picker_combo: The run these results belong to. This release has one run, Default; named runs, each with its own model, come later.
data.new_run_btn: Named runs come after the release.
data.manage_runs_btn: Named runs come after the release.
data.model_change_btn: Pick the model to run — your Step 2 and Step 3 models, Cellpose’s built-in ones, or a file.
data.row_tick: Ticked stacks are the ones Predict Selected and Reconstruct Selected run on; the two lists share the ticks.
data.row_chip: The model that made this stack’s result; amber when it is not the model now active, so a new Reconstruct would not match it.
data.row_eye: Show or hide this stack in the viewer.
data.start_from_combo: Fill the settings below from your Step 3 run or from a standard set; you can still change any of them.
data.chan1_combo: The channel the model reads as the cell membrane. A loaded or previewed stack shows its layer names here.
data.chan2_combo: The channel the model reads as the nuclei, or none. A loaded or previewed stack shows its layer names here.
data.cell_width_um_sb: About how wide one cell is, in micrometres; the model looks for cells near this size.
data.normalize_cb: Stretch each slice’s brightness before the model sees it.
data.rescale_cb: Used only when no cell width is set: when ticked, the image is passed to the model at its own scale; when unticked, the model resizes it by its own trained cell size. The factor used is recorded with the result.
data.predict_btn: Make the 2D outlines, slice by slice in all three views, for every ticked stack; the slow part, on the graphics card.
data.reconstruct_btn: Join each ticked stack’s 2D outlines into 3D cells; needs Predict first, and uses the 2D outlines already made.
data.cancel_btn: Stop after the stack being worked on; finished stacks are kept.
data.view_btn: Show the highlighted stack’s result in the viewer (the highlighted row, not the ticks); works while a run is going.
data.mt_row_click: Load this stack to measure and tidy it; if the loaded stack has unsaved edits you are asked first.
data.save_tiers_btn: Write this stack’s cells and measurements to disk; after this, Undo cannot go back further.
data.finalize_btn: Finalize saves this stack and marks it done, so Export takes it. It locks nothing.
data.export_btn: Opens the export window: features from every finalized stack, 3D meshes for the loaded stack.
data.export_row_tick: Finalized stacks that go into Export features; a stack that cannot go says why.
data.export_features_btn: Write one table of every cell from the finalized stacks, ready for your notebooks.
data.export_meshes_btn: Save each cell of the loaded stack as a 3D surface file for rendering or printing.
data.browse_workdir_btn: Choose the project folder. Every step reads and writes it.
data.add_folder_btn: Add every .tif stack in a folder to the list.
data.set_spacing_btn: Set the voxel size, the Z direction and the axis order of the ticked stacks.
data.extract_features_btn: Measure every cell of the loaded stack. The Workbench opens when it is done.
data.open_analysis_btn: Open the Workbench to look at the cells and mark them good or bad.
data.feature_reference_btn: List every measurement and what it means.
data.delete_bad_btn: Remove the cells marked bad. Undo can bring them back until you Save.
data.undo_btn: Take back the last Remove or Smooth, until you Save. The maps are not brought back: compute them again.
data.smooth_strength_combo: How strongly to round off the outlines.
data.smooth_all_btn: Smooth every cell’s outline. A cell too thin to survive is kept as it was.
data.fix_by_hand_btn: Fix cells by hand in 3D. This comes after the release.
data.smooth_sigma_z_sb: How far the smoothing reaches, up and down / across.
data.smooth_sigma_xy_sb: How far the smoothing reaches, up and down / across.
data.smooth_preserve_topology_cb: Keep each cell in one piece: if smoothing would split a cell, it is reconnected.
data.reset_original_btn: Put back the cells Reconstruct made. Your edits, measurements and exported 3D meshes are deleted.
data.batch_size_sb: How many slices go to the graphics card together; lower it if the card runs out of memory.
data.method_combo: The way the three views are joined into 3D cells. Only Direct is offered.
data.n_cpu_sb: How many processor cores the 3D build uses.
data.ps_smooth_probs_cb: Blur each view's cell-probability map before the views are joined, so cells do not step from slice to slice.
data.ps_smooth_flows_cb: Blur each view's flows before the views are joined.
data.ps_sigma_perp_sb: How far the blur reaches across the slices of each view; higher removes stripes between slices.
data.ps_sigma_inplane_sb: How far the blur reaches within a slice; keep it low to keep detail.
data.ps_mask_thresh_sb: Flows where the cell probability is below this are set to zero. Used only with Smooth the flows.
data.ps_soft_weight_cb: Scale the smoothed flows by how likely each voxel is inside a cell. Used only with Smooth the flows.
data.gd_decay_sb: How fast each step shrinks as voxels follow the flows; higher suits long, thin cells.
data.gd_iters_sb: How many steps each voxel takes along the flows.
data.gd_momenta_sb: How much of the previous step each step keeps (0 to 1). Rarely changed.
data.gd_renorm_cb: Set the flows back to unit length at every step.
data.gd_tile_z_sb: The depth of the pieces the volume is cut into for several cores. Used only with Use several cores.
data.gd_tile_y_sb: The height of those pieces. Used only with Use several cores.
data.gd_tile_x_sb: The width of those pieces. Used only with Use several cores.
data.gd_tile_overlap_sb: How much neighbouring pieces overlap, as a fraction. Used only with Use several cores.
data.ccp_ksize_sb: How many neighbouring voxels are pooled when the three views' probabilities are joined into 3D.
data.ccp_alpha_sb: A small count added before pooling so no single view dominates; higher evens the views out more.
data.ccp_smooth_sigma_sb: Blur the joined 3D cell mask before it is cut.
data.ccp_threshold_level_sb: Which automatic cut level decides whether a voxel is a cell; 0 is the lowest, and it must be below Number of levels minus 1.
data.ccp_threshold_n_levels_sb: How many bands the automatic threshold splits the probabilities into; there is one fewer level to choose from.
data.ccp_prob_thresh_sb: Set the cell-or-not cut by hand, from 0 to 1. Auto uses the two levels above.
data.ccp_min_prob_thresh_sb: The automatic cut never goes below this.
data.ccp_apply_one_d_p_cb: Round the automatic cut down to one decimal place.
data.post_small_obj_sb: Pieces of the 3D mask with fewer voxels than this are removed.
data.post_closing_sb: Close small gaps in the mask; the number is the size of the tool in voxels.
data.post_dilation_sb: Grow the mask outwards by this many voxels.
data.post_extra_erode_sb: Shrink the mask by this many voxels after the steps above.
data.ccg_ksize_sb: How many neighbouring voxels are pooled when the three views' flows are joined into 3D.
data.ccg_alpha_sb: A small count added before pooling so no single view dominates.
data.ccg_smooth_sigma_sb: Blur each view's flows before they are joined.
data.ccg_post_sigma_sb: Blur the 3D flows after they are joined.
data.cc_min_area_sb: Clusters of fewer voxels than this are not made into cells.
data.cc_thresh_factor_sb: Where points count as crowded: the average density plus this many spreads.
data.cc_smooth_sigma_sb: How much the point density is blurred before clusters are found.
data.sf_min_size_sb: Cells with fewer voxels than this are dropped.
data.sf_max_size_sb: Cells with more voxels than this are dropped.
data.sf_max_size_factor_sb: With the tick below: a cell larger than the average size plus this many spreads is dropped.
data.sf_do_stats_cb: Drop cells much larger than the typical cell, by the rule above.
data.do_mp_cb: Cut the volume into pieces and follow the flows on several cores at once.
data.skip_postprocess_cb: When ticked (the default), the final clean-up after the 3D build does not run, so the size limits below drop nothing. Untick it to apply them.
